entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:1
segments: Commandments--statutes--judgments; in this and some other places, commandments seem to mean the moral law, statutes the ceremonal, and judgments the judicial, or civil law.  In other cases they have a more general meaning, and comprehend the whole of God's commandments.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:3
segments: The commandments of God are all suited to promote industry, economy, temperance, and all those virtues which are conducive to health, long life, wealth, and happiness.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:4
segments: Though God is revealed as existing in three persons, yet is he one Jehovah.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:8
segments: Bind them for a sign--frontlets; figuratively spoken in the sense of, make yourselves familiar with them and remember them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:9
segments: All are bound to become familiarly acquainted with the commands of God, in order that through divine aid they may habitually and heartily obey them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:12
segments: Great prosperity, though it comes from God, is apt, through the wickedness of men, to lead them to forget and rebel against him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:13
segments: Swear by his name; in taking an oath on any proper occasion, they were not to appeal to idols or false gods, but only to Jehovah.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:14
segments: The gods of the people; idols and imaginary deities.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:16
segments: As ye tempted him in Massah;

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:21
segments: Children are naturally inquisitive, and parents should delight to communicate to them the information they need; expecially with regard to the character, works, and ways of God, that they may understand and do his will.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:23
segments: The land of Canaan, of which the children of Israel at the command of God took possession, was his gift to them.  In taking it from the Canaanites and giving it to the Israelites, he only did what he saw to be best with his own.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 6:25
segments:
Our righteousness; by observing and doing with a proper spirit what God commanded, they would for Christ's sake be accepted and treated as righteous. 
 
The way for men to be treated for Christ's sake as righteous, is to obey God; and they can have no evidence that they are accepted of him, any further than they are disposed to keep his commandments.
